rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (score 392.7, best so far). The oval now finishes in all 20 trials (mean 1.97 s, 0 line losses). That confirms the kp 5 / kd 1.0 change works on smooth track. The s-bend still ends off-track at progress 0.44, and the slalom reaches only 0.09 progress with 0.75 line-loss events per run. So the remaining failure is on sharper bends and direction changes, not on the straights. Two earlier results support this: raising kp and kd (iteration 3) moved s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.44, and ki changes did nothing (iteration 2). The line-loss events on the slalom suggest the robot is still steering too late or too weakly when the tape swings across the array. The change: raise kp from 5.0 to 6.0, which gives a stronger correction per millimetre of lateral error, and raise kd from 1.0 to 1.5, which damps the extra swing that the stronger kp will cause. Geometry and base_speed are held at iteration 3 values so the controller effect is isolated. ki stays at 0.2 because it has shown no benefit. Expected result: s-bend progress rises above 0.6, and slalom line-loss events drop below 0.5 per run. The oval should still finish. Risks: kp 6 with kd 1.5 could chatter. If steering_oscillation on the oval exceeds about 0.4, the next step is kp 5.5 with kd 1.5. If the oval finishes but the s-bend and slalom still exit the track, the next step is to test a lower base_speed (about 0.9) on the slalom-type bends. Hypotheses: H1, the controller is still under-correcting on sharp bends, so more kp helps. H2, the extra kd is needed to keep the stronger kp from oscillating. Measurements wanted next: progress and line_loss_events per track to see how far the slalom and s-bend runs get, steering_oscillation to check for chatter from higher kp and kd, and max_error to see whether the off-track margin is still being used up.
